To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rats with lesions of the fornix, which is known to carry the cholinergic fibers from the medial septum to the hippocampus, are severely impaired in a radial maze task in which the extramaze stimuli are varied across trials but are not impaired in a task in which the stimuli are fixed across trials.

fornix-transection impaired performance of rats on a distally, but not proximally, cued radial-maze task and that performance on this task varied with the location and stability, as well as the cholinergic integrity, of the stimuli.
fornix-transection impaired performance on a distal but not a proximal version of the radial arm maze task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of fornix lesions in a spatial memory task, and the role played by the cholinergic system in this task.
the functional role of the hippocampus in spatial learning and memory.
the effects of hippocampal lesions on spatial learning and memory in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fornix is involved in spatial memory, particularly when extramaze stimuli are present and the location of stimuli is not stable.
fornix lesions disrupt spatial memory when stimuli are distal and unstable.
the fornix-transection procedure causes a severe impairment on distal, but a transient or no impairment on proximal, radial maze cue tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

fornix transection impairs rats' performance in the V condition when stimuli are located in extramaze space and that the impairment is associated with a reduction of cholinergic input to the hippocampus.
the hippocampus is necessary for the processing of distal extramaze stimuli but not of proximal intramaze stimuli.
rats with hippocampal lesions were impaired on a distal cue task, whereas rats with fornix lesions were impaired on both a proximal and a distal cue tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fornix is involved in the processing of extramaze cues, and the hippocampus is not necessary for processing proximal visual stimuli.
fornix-transection affects rats' ability to learn the relative position of distal, but probably not of proximal, stimuli.
, in the radial maze, the relative position of stimuli is an important cue that can compensate for the loss of hippocampal function.
